fields.meta_description: Take a 7-question mattress quiz that names a bed type from how you sleep, then build one that matches shoppers to the beds you stock.
fields.h1: Build a Mattress Quiz That Matches Shoppers to Your Beds
fields.hero_description: Build a mattress quiz that matches each shopper to a bed you stock and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Mattress Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Describe your beds and your shoppers, and Emergent builds the questions, the matching, and the table where each result is saved.
fields.feature_1:
Questions about how people sleep

Name the beds you stock and what sets each apart, and Emergent drafts questions on sleep position, feel, bounce, and warmth. Change any question or option with a follow-up prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every option mapped to a bed

Each answer adds a point to one of your beds, and the bed with the most points becomes the shopper's result. When a new model arrives, one prompt adds it to the mapping.
fields.feature_3:
Answers saved in a database you own

Every finished quiz is a row with the shopper's answers, the result, and the date, in a database you own. Sort by result to see which bed the quiz recommended most this month.
fields.feature_4:
One question per phone screen

Shoppers answer one question per screen on a phone, from a link in an ad or a QR code on a showroom tag. Emergent puts no cap on how many shoppers take the quiz each month.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts when a lead needs a person

Set a rule, such as two partners far apart on firmness, and the app sends your sales team a Slack or email alert with their answers. Every other shopper goes on to the result.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, or the code itself

Run the quiz on your store's own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository for your developer.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Stores Run a Mattress Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
Quiz results put 58 shoppers in the showroom

Penlow Sleep Shop has 14 floor models and a 7-question quiz on its website. Each result names one of those beds, with a button to book a showroom visit. In October, 214 shoppers finished the quiz and 58 booked. Each booking names the matched bed, so staff have it made up before the shopper arrives.
fields.tab_content_2:
Hybrid replaces all-foam for hot sleepers

Hushwood Sleep Co. sells 3 mattresses online and saves each shopper's quiz answers with the order. This spring brought 31 returns, and 19 came from shoppers who said they sleep hot and were matched to the all-foam model. One prompt changed the mapping, and the quiz now sends hot sleepers to the hybrid.
fields.tab_content_3:
When partners differ by 3 points, sales steps in

Moorhaven Home's quiz asks each partner to rate the firmness they like on a 10-point scale. When the ratings differ by 3 or more, a salesperson gets a Slack alert with both sets of answers and calls the couple. In March, 23 of the 90 couples who took the quiz got that call.
fields.tab_content_4:
Reviews follow 512 soft foam results into April

The Pillow Ledger reviews mattresses and gives readers a quiz that names a bed type. A monthly email counts the results. March brought 1,240 takers: 512 landed on soft foam and 391 on hybrid. The editor put 3 soft foam models on April's review list.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Mattress Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a mattress quiz that recommends a bed from how people sleep, then improves it with real results.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the beds the quiz can recommend
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Map every option to one bed
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the beds, not the questions. Write down each model the quiz may recommend, with what it is made of and how firm it feels on your own scale. Four to six results is plenty, and the list goes straight into your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Shoppers know how they sleep far better than they know coil counts. Ask about sleep position, how warm they run, who shares the bed, and what bothers them about the mattress they own now. Give each question four options a shopper can pick at a glance.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each option one point toward one of your beds, and check that every bed collects points from at least two questions. Then take the quiz yourself as a side sleeper and as a back sleeper, and see whether each lands on the bed you would pick for that sleeper.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Firmness numbers are not comparable from one brand to the next. Describe the feel instead: sinks in, or stays flat. If you do show a number, call it your store's scale, and use that scale on every result and every floor tag.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Give each result one next step
fields.howto_step_5_des: Each result should name the bed, give one reason it fits drawn from the shopper's own answers, and offer a single next step, such as booking a visit or adding the bed to the cart. Pick the step that matches how your store sells.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Tie each result to the order
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask for an order number or an email address at the end. With it, every quiz result can be matched to what the shopper bought and whether it came back. Without that link you can count results, but you never learn which answers led to a return.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a month, put results beside returns and bookings. If one answer keeps leading to returns, move it to a different bed with a prompt, then let a full month of new results come in before you change anything else.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a mattress quiz for my store that asks how shoppers sleep and matches each one to a bed on my showroom floor.

faq_plan.a: A mattress quiz is a short set of questions about how a person sleeps, such as position, preferred feel, and how warm they run, that ends by recommending a mattress. On a store's website, each result names a type or one of the beds the store sells.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a mattress quiz?
faq_plan.a: Write a prompt that lists the beds you sell and the questions you want asked, and Emergent's AI survey builder builds the quiz, the logic that maps each answer to a bed, and the result screens. Take it yourself a few times, then publish it on your site.

faq_plan.q: Can I build a free mattress quiz for my store's website?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Keep the first version short, with five or six questions and one result per bed, and add questions once real shoppers have taken it.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a mattress quiz have?
faq_plan.hint: Do i need a new mattress quiz?
faq_plan.a: Six to eight questions is a good target. That is enough to separate four or five beds by sleep position, feel, warmth, and who shares the bed, and short enough to finish on a phone. Cut any question whose answers never change the result.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a mattress quiz ask shoppers?
faq_plan.a: Ask about things shoppers know firsthand: the position they fall asleep in, whether they like to sink in or lie on top, how warm they sleep, whether a partner shares the bed, and what they dislike about their current mattress. Leave out material specs they would have to look up.

faq_plan.q: Should a mattress quiz show firmness as a number or describe the feel?
faq_plan.a: Describe the feel, and add a number only if you define it. There is no universally accepted measurement for mattress firmness, and each manufacturer may use its own system. On a firmness scale, softer mattresses fall on the lower end. Label any number in your quiz as your store's own scale.

faq_plan.q: Which mattress types should a mattress quiz recommend?
faq_plan.a: Cover the types you sell, which for a general store means all-foam, innerspring, hybrid, and latex. A hybrid pairs an innerspring support core with a substantial comfort system on top, and a latex mattress is made entirely of latex rubber. Give each type its own result screen.

faq_plan.q: How should a mattress quiz handle couples who want different firmness?
faq_plan.a: Ask both partners the firmness question and compare the answers. When they sit far apart, point the result to beds that suit both, or send the couple to a salesperson. The app Emergent builds sends that alert to Slack or email, with both sets of answers attached.

faq_plan.q: Can a mattress quiz recommend specific models instead of mattress types?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Map each option to a model instead of a type, and the result screen can name the bed, its price, and where to try it. Keep four to six models in the quiz; more than that and two models end up sharing almost every answer.

faq_plan.q: How do I know if my mattress quiz recommendations are working?
faq_plan.a: Compare each result with what happened next: bookings, orders, and returns. A result that sells but comes back often is matching the wrong shoppers. With Emergent, every answer is stored in a database you own. Results sit next to your order records there, with no export from a separate quiz tool.
